title: Apply for mutual recognition of an interstate or New Zealand conveyancer licence
summary: This page explains how to apply for mutual recognition of an existing conveyancer licence from another state or New Zealand.
intro:
A conveyancer licence allows you to do legal work in relation to property transactions such as a sale or lease of land, or the granting of a mortgage.

If you want to apply for an individual conveyancer licence, and are seeking mutual recognition of your existing interstate or New Zealand conveyancing licence, you can do so online.
who_can_apply: Be a fit and proper person to hold a licence.
Meet the criteria regarding qualifications and experience.
Not be a 'disqualified person' under the Conveyancers Licensing Act 2003.
Have paid the relevant contribution to the Property Services Compensation Fund.
what_you_need: A certified copy of both sides of your valid interstate or New Zealand conveyancer licence (PDF or JPG format).
A completed Mutual recognition application form (PDF or JPG format).
Completed copies of your contact details (PDF or JPG format).
If trading under a business name, a copy of your ASIC business name certificate (PDF or JPG format).
A current credit card for payment.

how_to_steps.text: Gather your certificates and other documents.
Follow the prompts to apply for a conveyancer licence.
Download, print and complete the Application for an individual conveyancer licence – PDF.
Make sure you have the required documentation, and then visit a service centre and submit your application.

more_info.text: When applying for mutual recognition of an interstate or New Zealand conveyancer licence, you do not need to provide details of your qualifications, previous work experience, or nominate a referee, as part of your application for an individual conveyancer licence in NSW.

Licensed conveyancers must be covered by an approved policy of professional indemnity insurance when they work. A licensee can take out their own insurance policy, or they may be covered by their employer’s policy.

A person must not conduct a conveyancing business for fee or reward unless the person is the holder of a conveyancer's licence. (This does not apply to a person who is a solicitor or a barrister with a current practising certificate, or someone who conducts their conveyancing work in an incorporated legal practice, if that conveyancing work is overseen a barrister or solicitor.)
To make an application for an individual conveyancer licence in NSW without mutual recognition of an interstate or New Zealand conveyancer licence, visit Apply for a conveyancer licence – individual.

faqs.q: What does a conveyancer licence allow me to do?
faqs.a: A conveyancer licence allows you to perform legal work related to property transactions, such as selling or leasing land, or granting a mortgage.

faqs.q: Who is eligible to apply for mutual recognition?
faqs.a: You must be aged 18 or over, be a fit and proper person, meet qualification and experience criteria, and not be a 'disqualified person' under the Conveyancers Licensing Act 2003.

faqs.q: What documents do I need for mutual recognition?
faqs.a: You need a MyServiceNSW Account, a certified copy of both sides of your valid interstate or New Zealand licence, a completed Mutual recognition application form, and other required documents like your contact details and ASIC business name certificate (if applicable).
